Master eye and cross-dominance

Most people have a dominant (master) eye that the brain trusts more, usually on the same side as the dominant hand. The dominant eye should be the one looking along the rib, the flat strip on top of the barrels. With cross-dominance the dominant eye is on the other side from the shooting shoulder; with central vision neither eye clearly dominates. In both cases the gun points somewhere other than where you feel you are looking, often off to one side, so you miss without knowing why.

A simple test: with both eyes open, frame a distant object in a small triangle made with the hands. Then close each eye in turn: the eye that keeps the object in the triangle is dominant. A coach may also stand in front of the shooter and look through the triangle.

If eye and shoulder match, you can usually shoot with both eyes open. If not, the coach chooses a remedy. You can close or squint the other eye as the gun mounts, or put a small dot on the safety glasses. You can also learn to shoot from the other shoulder or, more rarely, use a cross-over stock, bent sideways so the other eye looks along the rib. The choice depends on age, experience and how strong the dominance is. Where possible, many coaches prefer both eyes open, because two eyes judge speed, angle and distance better.

Safety glasses are compulsory for shooters in both disciplines, so the dot goes on them.

Coaches often notice that a shooter’s eye dominance changes over the years, and some shooters feel a difference when they are tired. If you suddenly start missing to the same side again and again, recheck your master eye with your coach.

Where to look during the shot, a soft focus at the pick-up point and then a hard focus on the target, is explained in Eyes and attention: soft focus, hard focus and the quiet eye.

Key points

  • The dominant eye must look along the rib.
  • Cross-dominance and central vision make the gun point off target.
  • Test with a hand triangle; the coach chooses the remedy.
  • Safety glasses are compulsory in both disciplines.
  • Dominance can change; repeat the test.

Did you know?

The hand-triangle test works because, with both eyes open, the brain takes the aiming picture mostly from one eye. Close that eye and the object jumps out of the triangle.

Stand Talk

  • Coach Close your left eye as the gun comes up.

    Meaning: Shut the left eye during the mount, not before, so the right eye controls the gun.

  • Coach Eyes on the clay, not the barrel.

    Meaning: Keep looking at the target; checking the barrel usually slows or stops the gun.

  • Coach Look at the leading edge.

    Meaning: Focus on the front edge of the moving target, not its middle.

  • Coach Don't look at the trap — look out to your pick-up point.

    Meaning: Wait with the eyes a little out along the line, where the target is first seen clearly.

Check yourself · 3 questions

  1. A right-handed shooter has a left dominant eye. What is this called?

    1. Central vision
    2. Hard focus
    3. Cross-dominance
    4. Leading edge
    Answer

    Cross-dominance

    Cross-dominance is a dominant eye on the opposite side to the shooting shoulder.

  2. Why is looking back at the bead to check the lead a fault?

    1. It is forbidden by the rules of both disciplines
    2. It usually slows or stops the gun, so the shot goes behind
    3. The bead reflects the sun into the eye
    4. It makes the target change colour in flight
    Answer

    It usually slows or stops the gun, so the shot goes behind

    When you look at the gun instead of the target, the swing tends to slow or stop. The target slips to the edge of your vision, and the shot goes behind.

  3. Where does the anti-dominance dot usually go?

    1. On the safety glasses, in front of one eye
    2. On the bead at the end of the rib
    3. On the rib, halfway along it
    4. On the vest line, below the shoulder
    Answer

    On the safety glasses, in front of one eye

    Safety glasses are compulsory anyway, so a small dot on the lens in front of the non-dominant eye is the simplest remedy.
